title: P31: increase RoPE base from 10000 to 100000
description: P31: increase the rotary positional base tenfold while preserving all layers, heads, dimensions, initialization, and context lengths. Longer positional wavelengths may make citation relationships learned in short proofs transfer better to the longer proofs discovered by fixed downstream expert iteration.
hypothesis: No previous registration changes the RoPE base. Sharing blocks (014 and 028), extra heads (019), and RMSNorm (026) failed to beat the incumbent, often with similar token losses. Reducing angular variation in all but the highest-frequency rotary pair may favor longer-range citation relationships without reducing capacity or changing optimization. This is an unverified mechanism: weaker positional discrimination may instead hurt proof syntax and reference selection. The change persists into RL and evaluation, so this tests the architecture across stages rather than only the pretraining trajectory. Only the downstream three-seed dev-transfer metric decides keep/discard.
expected_delta: Central prediction +5 to +20 dev-transfer theorems at true length >=7 versus incumbent 012 (exact mean 147.67; stored rounded mean 148), with plausible downside -60. RoPE tensor shapes and operation counts are unchanged, so expect negligible per-step and per-token latency change and roughly 3000 pretraining updates in 300 seconds. Learned generation lengths can still affect total runtime under the unchanged 1200-second cap.

arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: Construct LongWavelengthGPT from the registered pretrain.py source with ROPE_BASE=100000, then load state. The inherited cfg and state dict do not encode the changed base. The live harness retains the subclass throughout RL and evaluation.
